methods.label: Enumerate the six arrangements
methods.explanation: The tree diagram gives \(3\times2\times1=6\) arrangements: 123, 132, 213, 231, 312, and 321. The numbers with 2 in the units place are 132 and 312, giving 2 even numbers. The probability is \(2/6=1/3\).
methods.levelReason: Listing six arrangements and reducing the resulting fraction require only elementary counting and Grade 9 probability.

methods.label: Consider only the units digit
methods.explanation: A number is even exactly when its units digit is even. In a random arrangement, each of the three cards is equally likely to occupy the units place, so the possible units digits 1, 2, and 3 each have probability \(1/3\). Only 2 is even, so the required probability is \(\frac13\).
methods.levelReason: The alternative uses equal likelihood of the units cards and the elementary units-digit test for evenness.
